The authors call the specimen nominally (Mg0.22Fe0.78)O or Mw78, then use room-pressure synchrotron Mossbauer spectroscopy to resolve 71.6 mol% high-spin Fe2+, 4.6 mol% high-spin Fe3+, 21.5 mol% Mg, and 2.3 mol% net cation vacancies per O: Mg0.215Fe2+0.716Fe3+0.046□0.023O. The EOS records are attached to that defect-normalized measured composition because both DAC fragments came from the same characterized crystal. The Fm-3m sites are an average diffraction proxy: the final article explicitly says the nominal cubic cell and Bragg peaks do not fully describe the diffuse defect structure, and it does not publish an ordered defect-cluster refinement. Room-pressure Mossbauer data establish high-spin Fe2+ and Fe3+ only at ambient pressure; this study did not measure spin state under compression, so neither EOS record is labeled as a high-spin pressure branch. The neon crystal becomes increasingly hexagonally distorted above about 20 GPa under growing differential stress. That high-pressure indexing-cell fit is documented but excluded from execution because no space group or atomic structure is established.

- **V0:** Final article, page 1713 and Table 3: 78.742(14) A^3 conventional cubic unit cell; fitted with ambient-volume prior 78.94 +/- 0.1 A^3
- **K0:** Final article, page 1713 and Table 3: K0T=163.0(1.0) GPa
- **K0 prime:** Final article, page 1713 and Table 3: K'0T=4.02(10), fitted under a 4.0 +/- 0.1 prior rather than fixed
- **Reference temperature (K):** Final article, Table 3 title: selected 300 K EOS fit parameters; nominal room-temperature reference
- **Volume basis:** Official deposit AM-17-85966, Table 2, Neon Medium - Cubic Unit Cell; the B1 conventional cell has Z=4
- **Uncertainties:** Final article, Figures 4 and 7 captions: 1-sigma fitting uncertainties; numerical covariance matrices are not printed

</details>

## Observation datasets

### magnesiowustite\_mw78\_finkelstein\_2017\_table2\_compression

- **Description:** Complete official Table 2 transcription for the defect-bearing Mw78 single crystal: one ambient row, 17 helium rows, and 12 neon rows, preserving both cubic and hexagonal cell indexings and the two ruby R1 wavelengths.
- **Kind:** pressure\_volume\_lattice\_parameters\_calibrant\_observations
- **Reference:**
    - **Authors:** Finkelstein; Jackson; Sturhahn; Zhang; Alp; Toellner
    - **Year:** 2017
    - **Title:** Single-crystal equations of state of magnesiowustite at high pressures
    - **Source:** American Mineralogist
    - **Volume:** 102
    - **Locator:** 1709-1717
    - **DOI:** 10.2138/am-2017-5966
- **Source location:** Official American Mineralogist deposit AM-17-85966, HarvestTable 2.pdf and HarvestTable 2.xlsx
- **Associated EOS records:** mg0215fe0762vac0023o\_finkelstein\_2017\_bm3\_helium\_1; mg0215fe0762vac0023o\_finkelstein\_2017\_bm3\_neon\_cubic\_2
- **Uncertainty:**
    - **Pressure:** The reported pressure uncertainty is the standard deviation of pressures from different ruby spheres in each chamber.
    - **Lattice and volume:** Parenthetical crystallographic uncertainties are transcribed in absolute units; c/a uncertainties are explicitly 1 sigma propagated from lattice-parameter fits.
    - **Missing:** The 19.244 GPa neon row has no printed pressure uncertainty and remains blank.
- **Notes:** The article's EOS fits use cubic volumes for all 17 helium rows, cubic volumes for the first five neon rows through 19.244 GPa, and hexagonal volumes for the seven neon rows from 24.084 GPa onward. The source also reports the unused alternate indexing at every pressure, retained here without cleaning. At 31.820 GPa helium, ruby 1 was estimated from ruby 2 using P\_ruby1=0.9973 P\_ruby2+1.8804 GPa because its wavelength was not measured. The official workbook omits a closing parenthesis in two 16.199(65) cells; the visually typeset official PDF confirms 16.199(65), which is transcribed here. The ambient footnote gives the geometric cubic-to-hexagonal transformation a\_hex=a\_cubic/sqrt(2), c\_hex=sqrt(3)a\_cubic, V\_hex=3V\_cubic/4.
